feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: ESMA Sets 2027 Work Priorities to Simplify and Integrate EU Capital Markets
entry.summary: ESMA sets 2027 priorities for stronger, simpler and more integrated EU capital markets ESMA · Sep 28, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has published its 2027 Annual Work Programme. It expands supervision of benchmark administrators and ESG rating providers, and advances simplification of reporting and supervisory frameworks. The plan also covers supervisory convergence for crypto-asset service providers under MiCA and the move to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027.[Generated summary]

entry.title: ESMA urges MiCA changes to clarify rules, strengthen safety and cover new crypto services
entry.summary: ESMA calls for changes to make MiCA clearer, safer and ready for emerging services ESMA · Sep 30, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority has responded to the European Commission's consultation on reviewing the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). It proposes simplifying the framework while strengthening investor protection, including stricter marketing rules and cost transparency. It also addresses decentralised finance, staking, lending and borrowing, and recommends stronger supervisory powers and binding token classification opinions.

entry.title: ESMA clarifies EU market participants' continued access to third-country CSD services
entry.summary: ESMA clarifies access for EU market participants to the services of third-country CSDs ESMA · Oct 7, 2026 ESMA has issued a statement saying EU market participants should not be blocked from using third-country central securities depositories beyond 17 January 2027 until the EU finalises legislation extending the transitional regime. The Market Integration and Supervision Package proposes a three-year extension, which the Council and European Parliament support. ESMA expects national authorities not to prioritise supervisory or enforcement action against unrecognised third-country CSDs until the extension takes effect.

entry.title: ESMA sets supervisory expectations for services linked to non-compliant stablecoins
entry.summary: ESMA sets out supervisory expectations on services related to unauthorised stablecoins ESMA · Oct 8, 2026 · Crypto The European Securities and Markets Authority has issued an opinion on crypto-asset services involving stablecoins (asset-referenced and e-money tokens) that do not comply with MiCA. It says MiCA-authorised crypto-asset service providers should stop providing services related to such non-compliant stablecoins to EU clients. National authorities should supervise market participants and require remediation of any remaining exposures within three months of publication.

entry.title: ESMA seeks feedback on tokenised collateral use in central clearing
entry.summary: ESMA seeks evidence on the use of tokenised collateral in central clearing ESMA · Oct 9, 2026 ESMA has launched a Call for Evidence on whether and under what conditions EU central counterparties could safely use tokenised collateral. The consultation covers how tokenisation may affect the transfer, management, protection and use of collateral throughout its lifecycle. Contributions are due by 15 January 2027, and ESMA will assess feedback in the first quarter of 2027.

entry.title: ESMA appoints Carlo Comporti as new Chair, taking office 1 November 2026
entry.summary: Carlo Comporti appointed Chair of the European Securities and Markets Authority ESMA · Oct 9, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority announced that Carlo Comporti has been appointed as its next Chair, confirmed by the Council of the European Union. He will take up the position on 1 November 2026. The release includes remarks from current Chair Verena Ross and a summary of Comporti's prior roles, including Commissioner at CONSOB and Secretary General of CESR.

entry.title: ESMA names Carlos San Basilio to its Management Board
entry.summary: ESMA appoints Carlos San Basilio as the new member of its Management Board ESMA · Oct 9, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has appointed Carlos San Basilio of Spain's CNMV as a new member of its Management Board. He replaces Carlo Comporti of Italy's CONSOB, who becomes ESMA Chair effective 1 November. The election took place at a Board of Supervisors meeting in Paris on 6 October 2026.

entry.title: ESMA issues thematic note on clear, fair and not misleading impact claims
entry.summary: ESMA promotes clarity in claims on impact and transition ESMA · Oct 12, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority published a third thematic note on impact claims made through funds and bonds. It explains that market participants understand positive environmental or social impact differently, and encourages them to clearly state what difference they expect to make, how they will generate impact, and how results will be measured. The note creates no new regulatory requirements; it offers observed market practices and examples to support understanding of existing expectations on clear, fair and not misleading communication.

entry.title: ESMA sets 2026 EU priorities for checking listed companies' annual financial reports
entry.summary: ESMA sets out 2026 European Common Enforcement Priorities ESMA · Oct 13, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has published its 2026 European Common Enforcement Priorities for annual financial reports of listed issuers. The priorities cover geopolitical risks and restructuring provisions under IFRS, materiality and connected information under ESRS sustainability reporting, and common filing errors in the statement of changes in equity under ESEF.

entry.title: EU supervisors publish 2027 work priorities
entry.summary: European Supervisory Authorities set priorities for 2027 ESMA · Oct 13, 2026 The Joint Committee of the EBA, EIOPA and ESMA published its 2027 Annual Work Programme. It sets priorities including digital operational resilience, consumer protection, sustainable finance, securitisation and cross-sectoral risk monitoring. The plan also covers oversight of critical ICT third-party providers under DORA and aims to reduce regulatory burden.

entry.title: ESMA report finds continued growth in cross-border investment services
entry.summary: ESMA analysis shows continued growth in cross-border investment services ESMA · Oct 14, 2026 ESMA and national competent authorities completed their annual analysis of 2025 cross-border investment services to retail clients across 30 EU/EEA jurisdictions. About 15.5 million retail clients received services from firms in other Member States, up 47% from 2024. Firms rose from 370 to 379 while complaints stayed broadly stable.

entry.title: ESMA's third sanctions report calls for more consistent enforcement across the EU
entry.summary: ESMA's third Sanctions Report highlights the need for greater convergence in enforcement ESMA · Oct 15, 2026 ESMA has published its consolidated report on sanctions and measures imposed across the EEA in 2025. National authorities imposed 955 administrative sanctions and measures, with total administrative fines of about €82 million, and Germany, France and Spain accounted for two thirds of the fine value. The report finds significant differences in enforcement across Member States and says ESMA will foster exchanges among national authorities so that similar breaches lead to similar outcomes across the EU.

entry.title: ESMA updates transparency manual with new OTC derivatives and tick-size guidance
entry.summary: ESMA updates its manual on transparency with new guidance for OTC derivatives and tick-size regime ESMA · Oct 15, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has updated its manual on pre- and post-trade transparency under MiFID II/MiFIR. The update gives further guidance on identifying over-the-counter derivatives subject to transparency requirements and on how their identifying reference data should be provided. It also adds published Q&As and recommendations on applying the tick-size regime.

entry.title: EU T+1 settlement: regulatory framework complete, one year before switchover
entry.summary: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen ESMA · Oct 16, 2026 The EU will switch to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027. ESMA has published revised guidelines on standardised procedures and messaging protocols, clarifying how investment firms and their clients must meet the new allocation and confirmation requirements from 7 December 2026. The requirements include mandatory electronic, standardised communication channels and machine-readable methods.

entry.title: ESMA finalises review of guidelines on delaying disclosure of inside information
entry.summary: ESMA finalises the review of guidelines on the delay in disclosure of inside information ESMA · Oct 16, 2026 ESMA has updated and streamlined its MAR guidelines on delaying the disclosure of inside information, completing the revised framework. The guidelines add five legitimate interests that can justify a delay, and remove those tied to protracted processes, since issuers no longer must disclose such information before completion from June 2026. The revised guidelines apply from their publication on ESMA's website in the 24 official EU languages.](

entry.title: ESMA publishes new Q&As on CCPs, crowdfunding and EMIR
entry.summary: New Q&As available ESMA · Oct 16, 2026 ESMA has published new Q&As covering central counterparties (CCPs), European crowdfunding service providers for business, the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), and EMIR. The Q&As address the AAR 85% exemption, AAR thresholds calculation and AAR representativeness obligation.

entry.title: ESMA sets requirements for safe use of post-trade risk reduction services
entry.summary: ESMA specifies requirements to facilitate safe use of post-trade risk reduction services ESMA · Oct 20, 2026 ESMA, the EU financial markets regulator, has set out the conditions providers and users of post-trade risk reduction (PTRR) services must meet for certain OTC derivative transactions to be exempt from the clearing obligation under EMIR 3. The final report also sets safeguards for providing these services and monitoring use of the exemption. The rules aim to facilitate PTRR services while ensuring the exemption is used under EMIR 3 conditions and the clearing obligation is not misused. The draft Regulatory Technical Standards will now go to the European Commission for endorsement.

entry.title: ESMA trims outdated market structure Q&As under simplification drive
entry.summary: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts ESMA · Oct 22, 2026 The European Securities and Markets Authority has updated its Q&As on market structure under MiFID II, MAR and the Short Selling Regulation. As part of its Simplification and Burden Reduction initiative, it removed outdated, duplicative or no longer relevant guidance, and several Q&As were withdrawn or amended. The aim is to reduce unnecessary complexity and keep guidance consistent with the current legislative framework.
